tryThisNow: Open one adviser note and run a two-minute audit: mark who bears the loss, how the adviser is paid, and whether the role is broker, adviser, or planner.

implementationPlan.title: Audit Advice Before Accepting It
implementationPlan.coreSkill: Use advice without surrendering judgment. Before accepting a recommendation, confirm that the capital owner still bears the outcome, identify whether compensation creates an incentive, and separate broker sales activity from ongoing fiduciary advice.

ifThenPlans.plan: If regulation makes an adviser feel automatically safe, then write in the notebook margin: legal status is a starting point, but the owner still bears the loss and must judge the advice.
If a recommendation arrives without a clear pay explanation, then post a team chat request for the compensation and scope questions before treating the advice as neutral.
If a broker, adviser, or planner label is being used as if all duties match, then pause the clinic handoff and check registration and disclosure records before relying on the role.

implementationPlan.twentyFourHourChallenge: Within the next day, pick one current or potential adviser and complete a two-minute audit: responsibility, compensation, and role. Leave the decision pending if any line is blank.
implementationPlan.weeklyPractice: Once a week, use a two-trigger checklist. Trigger one: before accepting advice, note who bears the loss and how the adviser is paid. Trigger two: before relying on a professional title, check whether the role is sales, ongoing advice, or planning.
